title: Infrastructure Red Teaming With Abliterated Models: What Actually Stops Agent Attacks
relevance_rationale: Directly presents empirical red-teaming results for agent infrastructure on Kubernetes, covering sandboxing, NetworkPolicy enforcement, injection classification, and the unsolved memory-poisoning gap (OWASP ASI06).
one_paragraph: Model refusal is not a containment boundary: a successful prompt injection bypasses alignment, so infrastructure controls must be validated independently of model behavior. To isolate that variable, the speaker abliterated a Qwen3.6-27B model served via vLLM, eliminating refusals so every probe actually reached the tool-dispatch layer and the surrounding Kubernetes infrastructure. title: Keynote: MCP and the Era of Connectivity
relevance_rationale: Directly addresses the role of open connectivity standards like MCP in enabling model‑tool interaction and outlines future directions for agent ecosystems.
one_paragraph: The keynote argues that as AI models grow more capable, they require reliable, standardized ways to interact with external tools, data sources, and services. David Soria Parra positions the Model Context Protocol (MCP) as an open‑source connectivity layer that lets models safely reach out beyond their training corpora. He reviews MCP’s evolution over the past two years, highlighting how it has enabled plug‑and‑play tool use while preserving security boundaries. Looking ahead, he calls for broader industry adoption of similar open standards to avoid fragmentation and to ensure interoperability

title: Keynote: Building the Internet of Agents in the Open
relevance_rationale: The synthesis captures the talk’s focus on open agent interoperability, security sandboxing, observability, and evaluation as described in the title and speaker’s emphasis.
one_paragraph: The keynote framed the 'Internet of Agents' as an open, interoperable ecosystem where autonomous agents discover, negotiate, and collaborate via standardized protocols. Mazin Gilbert emphasized that realizing this vision requires a shared foundation of trust, security, and sandboxed execution to prevent malicious behavior while preserving agent autonomy. He argued that existing AI model APIs must be extended with lightweight, language‑agnostic messaging layers akin to the Model Context Protocol to enable cross‑vendor agent chaining.
